passages.text: This is the burden against the Valley of Vision: What ails you now, that you have all gone up to the rooftops, O city of commotion, O town of revelry? Your slain did not die by the sword, nor were they killed in battle.
passages.sermon:
The Lord gave a message about the Valley of Vision.
The Valley of Vision is a place in Jerusalem.
The Lord spoke to the people there.
He asked, “What is wrong with you now?”
All of you have gone up to the rooftops.
You live in a city full of noise.
Your city is busy and loud.
Your city is full of celebration and joy.
But many people in your city have died.
They did not die by the sword.
They were not killed in battle.
passages.original: מַשָּׂ֖א גֵּ֣יא חִזָּי֑וֹן מַה־ לָּ֣ךְ אֵפ֔וֹא כִּֽי־ עָלִ֥ית כֻּלָּ֖ךְ לַגַּגּֽוֹת׃ תְּשֻׁא֣וֹת׀ מְלֵאָ֗ה עִ֚יר הֽוֹמִיָּ֔ה קִרְיָ֖ה עַלִּיזָ֑ה חֲלָלַ֙יִךְ֙ לֹ֣א חַלְלֵי־ חֶ֔רֶב וְלֹ֖א מֵתֵ֥י מִלְחָמָֽה׃

passages.text: All your rulers have fled together, captured without a bow. All your fugitives were captured together, having fled to a distant place.
passages.sermon:
The rulers of the city fled together.
Enemies did not use bows to capture them.
All the rulers were taken as prisoners.
All the people who tried to escape were also captured together.
They had run far away from the city.
The captors found them and took them prisoner.
passages.original: כָּל־ קְצִינַ֥יִךְ נָֽדְדוּ־ יַ֖חַד מִקֶּ֣שֶׁת אֻסָּ֑רוּ כָּל־ נִמְצָאַ֙יִךְ֙ אֻסְּר֣וּ יַחְדָּ֔ו מֵרָח֖וֹק בָּרָֽחוּ׃

passages.text: Therefore I said, “Turn away from me, let me weep bitterly! Do not try to console me over the destruction of the daughter of my people.”
passages.sermon:
The prophet Isaiah speaks to the people of Jerusalem.
He feels deep sorrow.
He says, “Turn away from me.
Let me weep with bitterness.
Do not try to comfort me.
My people have been destroyed.
I mourn for the daughter of my people.”
passages.original: עַל־ כֵּ֥ן אָמַ֛רְתִּי שְׁע֥וּ מִנִּ֖י אֲמָרֵ֣ר בַּבֶּ֑כִי אַל־ תָּאִ֣יצוּ לְנַֽחֲמֵ֔נִי עַל־ שֹׁ֖ד בַּת־ עַמִּֽי׃

passages.text: For the Lord GOD of Hosts has set a day of tumult and trampling and confusion in the Valley of Vision— of breaking down the walls and crying to the mountains.
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD of Hosts rules over all armies.
He has set a day.
This day brings turmoil.
This day brings trampling.
This day brings confusion.
This day happens in the Valley of Vision.
People break down the walls.
People cry out to the mountains.
passages.original: כִּ֣י יוֹם֩ מְהוּמָ֨ה וּמְבוּסָ֜ה וּמְבוּכָ֗ה לַֽאדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֛ה צְבָא֖וֹת בְּגֵ֣יא חִזָּי֑וֹן מְקַרְקַ֥ר קִ֖ר וְשׁ֥וֹעַ אֶל־ הָהָֽר׃

passages.text: Elam takes up a quiver, with chariots and horsemen, and Kir uncovers the shield.
passages.sermon:
Elam is a nation.
Elam takes up a quiver.
Elam brings chariots.
Elam brings horsemen.
Kir is another nation.
Kir uncovers the shield.
passages.original: וְעֵילָם֙ נָשָׂ֣א אַשְׁפָּ֔ה בְּרֶ֥כֶב אָדָ֖ם פָּֽרָשִׁ֑ים וְקִ֥יר עֵרָ֖ה מָגֵֽן׃

passages.text: Your choicest valleys are full of chariots, and horsemen are posted at the gates.
passages.sermon:
The people of Jerusalem see their best valleys.
These valleys are full of chariots.
Horsemen stand at the city gates.
The enemy fills the land with soldiers and horses.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֥י מִבְחַר־ עֲמָקַ֖יִךְ מָ֣לְאוּ רָ֑כֶב וְהַפָּ֣רָשִׁ֔ים שֹׁ֖ת שָׁ֥תוּ הַשָּֽׁעְרָה׃

passages.text: He has uncovered the defenses of Judah. On that day you looked to the weapons in the House of the Forest.
passages.sermon: God uncovered the defenses of Judah.\r\nOn that day, you looked at the weapons in the House of the Forest.
passages.original: וַיְגַ֕ל אֵ֖ת מָסַ֣ךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה וַתַּבֵּט֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא אֶל־ נֶ֖שֶׁק בֵּ֥ית הַיָּֽעַר׃

passages.text: You saw that there were many breaches in the walls of the City of David. You collected water from the lower pool.
passages.sermon:
You saw the City of David.
You saw its walls.
You saw many breaches in the walls.
You gathered water.
You took water from the lower pool.
passages.original: וְאֵ֨ת בְּקִיעֵ֧י עִיר־ דָּוִ֛ד רְאִיתֶ֖ם כִּי־ רָ֑בּוּ וַֽתְּקַבְּצ֔וּ אֶת־ מֵ֥י הַבְּרֵכָ֖ה הַתַּחְתּוֹנָֽה׃

passages.text: You counted the houses of Jerusalem and tore them down to strengthen the wall.
passages.sermon: The people of Jerusalem counted the houses in the city.\r\nThey tore down the houses.\r\nThey used the materials to make the city wall stronger.
passages.original: וְאֶת־ בָּתֵּ֥י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם סְפַרְתֶּ֑ם וַתִּתְֿצוּ֙ הַבָּ֣תִּ֔ים לְבַצֵּ֖ר הַחוֹמָֽה׃

passages.text: You built a reservoir between the walls for the waters of the ancient pool, but you did not look to the One who made it, or consider Him who planned it long ago.
passages.sermon:
The people of Jerusalem built a reservoir.
They placed it between the city walls.
They made it to collect water from the ancient pool.
They did not look to God.
God made the pool.
They did not consider God.
God planned the pool long ago.
passages.original: וּמִקְוָ֣ה׀ עֲשִׂיתֶ֗ם בֵּ֚ין הַחֹ֣מֹתַ֔יִם לְמֵ֖י הַבְּרֵכָ֣ה הַיְשָׁנָ֑ה וְלֹ֤א הִבַּטְתֶּם֙ אֶל־ עֹשֶׂ֔יהָ וְיֹצְרָ֥הּ מֵֽרָח֖וֹק לֹ֥א רְאִיתֶֽם׃

passages.text: On that day the Lord GOD of Hosts called for weeping and wailing, for shaven heads and the wearing of sackcloth.
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD of Hosts is the ruler of heaven’s armies.
On that day, the Lord GOD of Hosts gave a command.
He called the people to weep.
He called them to wail.
He called them to shave their heads.
He called them to wear sackcloth.
passages.original: וַיִּקְרָ֗א אֲדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֛ה צְבָא֖וֹת בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא לִבְכִי֙ וּלְמִסְפֵּ֔ד וּלְקָרְחָ֖ה וְלַחֲגֹ֥ר שָֽׂק׃

passages.text: But look, there is joy and gladness, butchering of cattle and slaughtering of sheep, eating of meat and drinking of wine: “Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die!”
passages.sermon:
The people felt joy and gladness.
They killed cattle.
They slaughtered sheep.
They ate meat.
They drank wine.
They said, “Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die.”
passages.original: וְהִנֵּ֣ה׀ שָׂשׂ֣וֹן וְשִׂמְחָ֗ה הָרֹ֤ג׀ בָּקָר֙ וְשָׁחֹ֣ט צֹ֔אן אָכֹ֥ל בָּשָׂ֖ר וְשָׁת֣וֹת יָ֑יִן אָכ֣וֹל וְשָׁת֔וֹ כִּ֥י מָחָ֖ר נָמֽוּת׃

passages.text: The LORD of Hosts has revealed in my hearing: “Until your dying day, this sin of yours will never be atoned for,” says the Lord GOD of Hosts.
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD of Hosts is the ruler of all heavenly armies.
The Lord GOD of Hosts spoke to me.
He revealed a message directly to me.
He said this about your sin.
Your sin will never be forgiven.
You will not receive atonement for this sin.
This will remain true until the day you die.
The Lord GOD of Hosts has declared this.
passages.original: וְנִגְלָ֥ה בְאָזְנָ֖י יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת אִם־ יְ֠כֻפַּר הֶעָוֺ֨ן הַזֶּ֤ה לָכֶם֙ עַד־ תְּמֻת֔וּן אָמַ֛ר אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃פ

passages.text: This is what the Lord GOD of Hosts says: “Go, say to Shebna, the steward in charge of the palace: What are you doing here, and who authorized you to carve out a tomb for yourself here—to chisel your tomb in the height and cut your resting place in the rock?
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD of Hosts speaks.
He gives a command.
He says, "Go to this steward."
The steward is Shebna.
Shebna is in charge of the palace.
Say to Shebna, "What are you doing here?"
Say, "Who gave you permission to be here?"
Say, "Why have you carved a tomb for yourself here?"
Say, "You have chiseled your tomb on high."
Say, "You have cut your resting place in the rock."
passages.original: כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֛ר אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה צְבָא֑וֹת לֶךְ־ בֹּא֙ אֶל־ הַסֹּכֵ֣ן הַזֶּ֔ה עַל־ שֶׁבְנָ֖א אֲשֶׁ֥ר עַל־ הַבָּֽיִת׃ מַה־ לְּךָ֥ פֹה֙ וּמִ֣י לְךָ֣ פֹ֔ה כִּֽי־ חָצַ֧בְתָּ לְּךָ֛ פֹּ֖ה קָ֑בֶר חֹצְבִ֤י מָרוֹם֙ קִבְר֔וֹ חֹקְקִ֥י בַסֶּ֖לַע מִשְׁכָּ֥ן לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Look, O mighty man! The LORD is about to shake you violently. He will take hold of you, roll you into a ball, and sling you into a wide land. There you will die, and there your glorious chariots will remain—a disgrace to the house of your master.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts speaks to Shebna, the steward in charge of the palace.
Shebna is a powerful man.
The LORD will shake you, Shebna, with great force.
He will seize you.
He will wrap you up tightly, like a ball.
He will throw you into a distant and wide land.
You will die there.
Your glorious chariots will stay there.
Your master’s house will be disgraced because of you.
passages.original: הִנֵּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ מְטַלְטֶלְךָ֔ טַלְטֵלָ֖ה גָּ֑בֶר וְעֹטְךָ֖ עָטֹֽה׃ צָנ֤וֹף יִצְנָפְךָ֙ צְנֵפָ֔ה כַּדּ֕וּר אֶל־ אֶ֖רֶץ רַחֲבַ֣ת יָדָ֑יִם שָׁ֣מָּה תָמ֗וּת וְשָׁ֙מָּה֙ מַרְכְּב֣וֹת כְּבוֹדֶ֔ךָ קְל֖וֹן בֵּ֥ית אֲדֹנֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: I will remove you from office, and you will be ousted from your position.
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD of Hosts speaks to Shebna.
Shebna is the steward in charge of the palace.
God says, "I will remove you from your office."
I will take away your position.
You will lose your place of authority.
passages.original: וַהֲדַפְתִּ֖יךָ מִמַּצָּבֶ֑ךָ וּמִמַּעֲמָֽדְךָ֖ יֶהֶרְסֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: On that day I will summon My servant, Eliakim son of Hilkiah.
passages.sermon:
God speaks in this passage.
God promises to act on a specific day.
God says, “On that day, I will call My servant.”
God identifies His servant as Eliakim.
Eliakim is the son of Hilkiah.
God will summon Eliakim, son of Hilkiah, to serve Him.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֖ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא וְקָרָ֣אתִי לְעַבְדִּ֔י לְאֶלְיָקִ֖ים בֶּן־ חִלְקִיָּֽהוּ׃

passages.text: I will clothe him with your robe and tie your sash around him. I will put your authority in his hand, and he will be a father to the dwellers of Jerusalem and to the house of Judah.
passages.sermon:
God speaks about Eliakim son of Hilkiah.
God will clothe Eliakim with your robe.
God will tie your sash around Eliakim.
God will give your authority to Eliakim.
Eliakim will become a father to the people living in Jerusalem.
Eliakim will become a father to the house of Judah.
passages.original: וְהִלְבַּשְׁתִּ֣יו כֻּתָּנְתֶּ֗ךָ וְאַבְנֵֽטְךָ֙ אֲחַזְּקֶ֔נּוּ וּמֶֽמְשֶׁלְתְּךָ֖ אֶתֵּ֣ן בְּיָד֑וֹ וְהָיָ֥ה לְאָ֛ב לְיוֹשֵׁ֥ב יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם וּלְבֵ֥ית יְהוּדָֽה׃

passages.text: I will place on his shoulder the key to the house of David. What he opens no one can shut, and what he shuts no one can open.
passages.sermon:
God speaks about Eliakim son of Hilkiah.
God will give Eliakim the key to the house of David.
God will place this key on Eliakim’s shoulder.
Eliakim will have authority over the house of David.
If Eliakim opens something, no one can shut it.
If Eliakim shuts something, no one can open it.
passages.original: וְנָתַתִּ֛י מַפְתֵּ֥חַ בֵּית־ דָּוִ֖ד עַל־ שִׁכְמ֑וֹ וּפָתַח֙ וְאֵ֣ין סֹגֵ֔ר וְסָגַ֖ר וְאֵ֥ין פֹּתֵֽחַ׃

passages.text: I will drive him like a peg into a firm place, and he will be a throne of glory for the house of his father.
passages.sermon:
God speaks about a chosen man.
God will make this man secure and steady.
God will fix him firmly, like a peg in a strong place.
This man will become a throne of honor.
He will bring glory to his father's house.
passages.original: וּתְקַעְתִּ֥יו יָתֵ֖ד בְּמָק֣וֹם נֶאֱמָ֑ן וְהָיָ֛ה לְכִסֵּ֥א כָב֖וֹד לְבֵ֥ית אָבִֽיו׃

passages.text: So they will hang on him the whole burden of his father’s house: the descendants and the offshoots—all the lesser vessels, from bowls to every kind of jar.
passages.sermon:
God chose a man to carry responsibility for his father's house.
They will place on him all the honor of his father's family.
This includes the descendants.
This includes the offshoots.
They will hang on him every small vessel.
This means every kind of bowl.
This means every kind of jar.
He will bear the full weight of his family's legacy.
passages.original: וְתָל֨וּ עָלָ֜יו כֹּ֣ל׀ כְּב֣וֹד בֵּית־ אָבִ֗יו הַצֶּֽאֱצָאִים֙ וְהַצְּפִע֔וֹת כֹּ֖ל כְּלֵ֣י הַקָּטָ֑ן מִכְּלֵי֙ הָֽאַגָּנ֔וֹת וְעַ֖ד כָּל־ כְּלֵ֥י הַנְּבָלִֽים׃

passages.text: In that day, declares the LORD of Hosts, the peg driven into a firm place will give way; it will be sheared off and fall, and the load upon it will be cut down.” Indeed, the LORD has spoken.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts speaks.
He says, “In that day, the peg will move.”
This peg was driven into a firm place.
The peg will be cut off.
The peg will fall.
The load on the peg will be removed.
The LORD has spoken.
passages.original: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא נְאֻם֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת תָּמוּשׁ֙ הַיָּתֵ֔ד הַתְּקוּעָ֖ה בְּמָק֣וֹם נֶאֱמָ֑ן וְנִגְדְּעָ֣ה וְנָפְלָ֗ה וְנִכְרַת֙ הַמַּשָּׂ֣א אֲשֶׁר־ עָלֶ֔יהָ כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבֵּֽר׃ס
